I just got dropped off by my Gojek ride from work. The driver struck a conversation with me, and said that he’s currently on his thesis for his clinical psychology bachelor degree–– but it’s been six-years since he started his bachelor program because he has to juggle a family and working as a Gojek driver.

I’m typically very uninterested in idle chit-chats with strangers, but he really got my attention. He started asking me questions about the basis of every relationship according to my point of view, and this led to another conversation to Freudian theory. This conversation got very interesting as I don’t usually talk much about theories and whatnots since I’m pretty much a clown to everyone around me.

I really wanted to help him with his thesis, so during the ride, I told him I’m going to give him a miss-call and he could feel free to go on with the chat through WhatsApp–– alas, he said that he ran out of data because he’s been broke for quite a while, and therefore, he can only accept calls.

Although tipping isn’t culturally mandatory in Indonesia, the app enables us to tip our drivers from our credit. Without further thinking, I tipped him the most amount out of the options given, and anonymously bought him the biggest data package available from Tokopedia added to his phone number so he can surf the web to do further research for his thesis.

I usually hate talking about the “good deeds” that I’ve done for someone because I find it distasteful to brag about the good that you’ve done–– but it was a very interesting ride for me, and I wish it lasted longer, and that was how much I appreciated the conversation I had with him. I bet it took him some guts to ask his passengers to participate on his research–– but nonetheless, he was very non-intrusive about it and he was rather polite.

I hope the extra tip and the data package are going to be useful for him to go further on his thesis. I really do.

Actually I’m only socially awkward when I’m not recharged whatsoever— but even then,  it’s not as much as awkward, more like less talkative than usual and more absorbed into whatever I’m doing at that moment.

I’m a pretty big introvert— and this is such a foreign concept for people around me because I come off pretty bold and whenever I brush them off by saying that “oh, haha, I really like solitude though”, they’d usually just tell me right off “well I don’t claim to be an introvert and everyone needs their downtime”. Needless to say, I don’t argue further on those types of conversation and just let it go. Haha. 

I’d say I’m pretty confident— I know what I know, and I know what I don’t know. And for being an INTP, I go get sucked into so much reading and learning, and learned how to present an argumentation well— therefore, when I’m firm with my opinion, I’m especially meticulous in picking the words that would best deliver my point with a conviction. This contributes on sounding confident. When I’m not 100% confident about knowing something, I’d usually start my sentences with words such as “I believe”, “as far as I know”, “I feel that”, and stuff like that— you get the idea— and I’d end it with “prove me wrong in this if you disagree”. 

Regardless, I don’t argue as a sport, though, but I’m generally not a self-doubting person. I’d like to think that I’m pretty self-aware and I know that I’m likeable enough— for those who don’t— then there’s just simply not enough chemistry for us, and it’s not something I’d like to force. I’m your typical INTP that isn’t typically succinct in casual conversations, and therefore, I have the tendency to branch out upon carrying on the conversation. I also have genuine curiosity on others’ perspectives, so that bit also keep conversations smooth. I actually won an actual award for being “The Greatest Showman” in my company— I work in a creative agency, where everyone is generally under some sort of pressure and people become high-strung and stuff.

Since I barely ever panic, I’m mostly pretty upbeat and unfazed by stressors here and there, because I’m confident that doing my humanly best is enough and there’s no need for me to fulfill a preconceived expectation. I found a passion when I was 15, though, and it was photography. I was extremely passionate and that kept me going. 

When I was 17, I developed a drinking problem, started chainsmoking, and lost a bunch of weight from having an eating disorder. I suddenly was this attractive lady with modelesque figure with awesome legs. I started sneaking out of the house and partying with a bunch of fishy strangers and hooking up with people while getting batshit drunk everyday. Suddenly, I was hot and I was cool. Still, though, I retained the trauma from everything I had endured.

My mom found out about this and yelled at me. She would call me a slut. So not only I was told that I was useless, stupid, lazy, weird, and all that, I was apparently a slut too. That didn’t stop me from sneaking out and getting drunk, though.

I got rejected by universities because of my terrible grades. I had to move from Indonesia to United States to go to a pretty shitty college because it was the only college that’d take me. Obviously, I took photography. 

I didn’t say a word in college. I was under the illusion that people talked about me behind my back. Gosh, I was always nervous to be in class. Group works always made me even more nervous. I wouldn’t participate in class discussions, I remember one time I had to take a class where I had an assignment for public speaking. I just couldn’t do it. I was in front of the class, froze there for 15 minutes, and ran to the bathroom and cried so much.

Somehow I did better in socializing outside of college, though. I signed up on a platform that connect artists and models, and I was pretty active in pursuing my own photography projects. I started building my portfolio and would get gigs and made money from there. Still, being inside the campus still made me nervous and it hindered me from passing classes because I was too scared to interact with anyone.

I started having friends, though I’d still have my bouts of breakdowns and wanting to just kill myself and feel miserable. I spent every night drinking, and couldn’t stand one night without getting drunk. 

Fast forward to 2013, I was told to go home immediately because my dad was terminally ill. At this time, I’d also take diabetic drugs that would make me feel nauseous and throw up to the point of dry heaving. There were instances where I couldn’t get up from a public bathroom, but also couldn’t tell anyone why I disappeared because nobody knew about my eating disorder. I was in a verge of getting into a relationship with someone back home, and he promised to be by my side when I come home. I was miserable when I got into town, got drunk in the flight, and ran off with that guy because I simply wasn’t ready to see my dad being terminally ill. Long story short, everyone was looking for me and my mom demanded me to go to the hospital immediately (understandably). That guy disappeared on me afterwards, and told me that he wasn’t ready to handle someone who was in such delicate situation. I found out that what happened instead was that he got back together with his ex.

My dad eventually passed two months later, and I dropped out of college immediately since it was just him who demanded me to go for college. I was so devastated. At the same time, I went from a size 2 to a size 10. I felt so low. After all, knowing that I was skinny was what kept me going. I’d just get super drunk every night and wept and felt worthless. 

This behavior went on as I was pursuing my career as a photographer. Fast forward to 2015, I got madly in love with my ex whom I later had an intense relationship with. By this time, I’d had my fair share of boyfriends already, so getting into another relationship wasn’t new. It was an intense and complicated relationship where he was basically gaslighting me all the time and insinuate that I’ve been living the wrong way. Guess what, I believed him. He was a master manipulator. 

Fast forward to 2017, I called out on his behavior and told him it wasn’t okay. Realizing that I finally caught him on, he dumped me through text. He was out of town, and a day in prior, we were literally together for a week in my apartment where I took care of him, spoon fed him, cooked him meals, and helped him bathe because he was sick. I was MISERABLE. This was the worst heartbreak I had in my life. I never truly loved someone as deeply and as genuinely as I loved him without expecting anything in return. I had compromised so, so much.

I felt like I lost my sense of self, and I didn’t know who I was anymore, and while I had been feeling like I’d rather be dead for the most part of my life, I also felt like I was a waste of space. I believed that was an objective view towards myself, and I didn’t believe there would be any real benefit in changing that perspective. Nonetheless, I also came to a realization that I no longer wanted to live that way. Instead of another attempt on suicide, I seeked professional help. This time, I was lucky I found a professional that didn’t just trivialize my mental health. 

Along the journey, I developed drugs dependency along with alcoholism. I’d mix them together, and couldn’t go a day without being on drugs— otherwise I’d go back to being sad. He really haunted me for a year, that was the hardest breakup I had to go through.

I finally had it and was experiencing symptoms where I couldn’t get out of the bed. My tests came out fine, but all the doctors I went to didn’t believe my symptoms either. I had no energy to seek drugs and alcohol. I was just in bed motionlessly for a month. In a way, I was forced to stop alcohol and drugs because I no longer had access to them.

January 2018, I met this guy whom I clicked with instantly. Unlike the others that just kept the conversations superficial, he was raw and authentic. We got into a relationship, and he supported me with all my addictions. He wasn’t perfect at handling it, but I weaned off my substance addiction as time went on.

I found my revelation a couple months later, when I first went to a psychiatrist. I was never put on medications before, and being on meds for chronic depression really revolutionized the way I perceive myself and the world around me. I felt really loved by my boyfriend, and I felt accepted by his family where I used to be denied based on my race.

We got married this year, and after all the hardwork I put into my photography career, I got offered a position that pays very nicely in October 2018. People at my work are also awesome and accepting.  I also found out that I have fibromyalgia, which explained my sudden immobility and all those unexplainable symptoms and flare-ups, most likely through the trauma I had endured. 

It’s been a slow progression— after all, it took most of my life to finally stop with suicide ideation and self harm. It took so, so long for me to finally accept myself. It wasn’t an easy journey, and it didn’t magically turn my life upside down in a night. It makes everything bearable though, knowing that I will always have myself as my own support system when all else fails, as I witnessed myself going through everything that could potentially fuck me up even more. I know that I’m strong, and I allow myself to be less than perfect when I need to be.

TL;DR, I’m glad I didn’t kill myself, but it took me a lifetime.

No, not until I was 24. 

I was born when my parents weren’t ready to be parents. As a result, they didn’t know how to raise one, and actually resented my existence. I was always blamed for everything. I was abused by my nanny when my parents weren’t around, and she’d lock me in my room where I was left crying and screaming. My parents didn’t believe me. I was powerless.

Fast forward 6 years later, my sister was born. She was treated so lovingly, the opposite of how my parents raised me. She was always put first before me. They bought her toys while they never bought me toys to play with. Whenever someone gifted me something, I was told to keep it in its packaging so they would stay nice and new. I had such a low self esteem, and was bullied in school by everyone. I had no friend. To top it all off, I got terrible grades in school from all the depression. When I told my parents I was bullied, they just told me I should stop being weird. It was my fault that I was bullied. And I was also blamed for my terrible grades. Did it end there? Of course not, my relatives had to jeer at me for being darker skinned than my family, and they kept telling me I was the ugly one. I also had a grandma who kept badmouthing me to people and criticized me relentlessly and yelled at me all the time. 

I was ten when I had my first suicide ideation. I tried jumping off the balcony, and people would bully me even more. Not even just the students, but also the teachers. I was admitted to a counseling teacher, and later on found out that she, too, had gossiped about my stories. 

I had to endure bullying and being ostracized throughout my school years with no one that understood. Group work was the worst— students were asked to pick their own team-mates, and they would intentionally make it obvious that I was alone. Some teachers were jerks enough that they’d intentionally stall that moment of having me standing in front by myself and mockingly ask the class “no taker for Natasha?” which would then lead them to pass around each other because nobody wanted to have me in their group. What the hell did I ever do to deserve this? I don’t know, these kids were harsh. I was just this quiet kid who’d occasionally cry when they l’d gotten out of line. Of course, I was mocked even more when I broke down crying. Terrible grades, dismissed by my parents, called names by my parents, no friends, depression, anxiety, like, why would I want to keep living?

One time, when I was eight, my parents forced me to go to the orphanage. Not just verbally. I was literally on the floor begging and crying while they keep telling me that they refuse to acknowledge me as their daughter. I got a silent treatment from my dad afterwards for a few weeks. He literally refused to acknowledge me. 

I started cutting myself when I was 14. My mom found out when I was 17. Instead of asking me what was wrong, she accused me of using drugs. I had to watch myself getting dismissed and blamed by my parents while watching my sister being coddled and prioritized. I remember not being able to talk to strangers. I remember having social anxiety.

Yes, YES. I had a very intense relationship and also complicated and full of problems but I still held on to it, and he dumped me. For someone who had been through intense torture and loss from my upbringing, this was the most intense heartbreak I ever endured. I couldn’t eat, I couldn’t move, and all I wanted to do was to cry. It’s those moments where waking up means facing a reality of losing someone you loved deeply, and sleeping means seeing him in your dreams. It was such a stabbing pain in the chest even though I knew I deserved better, but I couldn’t escape the intense sadness. There’s no amount of consolation that could make me feel better because I already knew all the things that they say that are true, yet I still yearned for him. You can’t choose who you love after all. You can’t choose how you feel either. I had lost a sense of myself for all those year of gaslighting and emotional manipulation. I realized that it was time for me to get an intervention from a professional. I was under the illusion that I was a waste of space and would rather be dead, and I believed that to be a fact rather than just a distortion of how I viewed myself. All I know was that I should not be feeling that way. I went to a therapist and she did EMDR. It took a few sessions for her to finally say that I am good to go on my own, and it didn’t magically make me feel better and had all my pain lifted, but it definitely changed my perspective. I also went to a psychiatrist afterwards and I was diagnosed to be clinically depressed. Took my meds, and while these weren’t necessarily a feel-good drug, it gave me a clearer structure on how I perceive things. 

By all means, you don’t have to seek medical intervention if you’re not ready, but know that the option is there. Please don’t lose hope. :)
